# Introduction

This comprehensive visualization guide, created by **Zaoqu Liu**, demonstrates advanced plotting techniques for cytokine activity data generated by **scaper**. We cover heatmaps, dimensionality reduction plots, correlation analyses, and integration with Seurat's visualization ecosystem.

# Setup and Data Preparation

```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
library(scaper)
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)
library(pheatmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
library(RColorBrewer)

# Load and prepare data
data(pbmc_small)

# Compute cytokine activities (normalize=TRUE handles normalization)
cytokine_result <- scapeForSeurat(
  seurat.object = pbmc_small,
  database = "cytosig",
  cytokine = "all",
  normalize = FALSE
)

# Extract activity matrix
activity_matrix <- t(as.matrix(
  GetAssayData(cytokine_result, assay = "scape", layer = "data")
))

cat(sprintf("Computed activity for %d cytokines across %d cells\n", 
            ncol(activity_matrix), nrow(activity_matrix)))
```

# Heatmap Visualizations

## Basic Heatmap

```{r heatmap_basic, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Sample cytokines for clarity
set.seed(42)
sample_cyts <- sample(colnames(activity_matrix), 20)
plot_data <- activity_matrix[, sample_cyts]

pheatmap(
  t(plot_data),
  fontsize_row = 8,
  fontsize_col = 6,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "firebrick3"))(100),
  main = "Cytokine Activity Heatmap (20 Cytokines)",
  border_color = NA
)
```

## Hierarchical Clustering Heatmap

```{r heatmap_clustered, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
# Use all cytokines, cluster to find patterns
pheatmap(
  t(activity_matrix),
  fontsize_row = 5,
  fontsize_col = 5,
  clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "#F7F7F7", "#B2182B"))(100),
  main = "Complete Cytokine Activity Landscape",
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  border_color = NA
)
```

## Annotated Heatmap with Cell Type

```{r heatmap_annotated, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Create annotation for cells (using Seurat idents as example)
cell_annotation <- data.frame(
  CellType = Idents(pbmc_small),
  row.names = colnames(pbmc_small)
)

# Select top variable cytokines
cytokine_vars <- apply(activity_matrix, 2, var)
top_cyts <- names(sort(cytokine_vars, decreasing = TRUE)[1:25])

pheatmap(
  t(activity_matrix[, top_cyts]),
  annotation_col = cell_annotation,
  fontsize_row = 7,
  fontsize_col = 4,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  main = "Top 25 Variable Cytokines by Cell Type",
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  border_color = NA
)
```

# Distribution Visualizations

## Activity Distribution Across Cytokines

```{r distribution, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Prepare data for boxplot
selected_cyts <- c("IL6", "IFNG", "IL4", "TNFA", "IL2", "IL10", "TGFB1", "IL13")
plot_data_box <- activity_matrix[, selected_cyts]

# Create boxplot
boxplot(plot_data_box, 
        col = rainbow(length(selected_cyts)),
        main = "Activity Score Distributions",
        ylab = "Activity Score [0, 1]",
        xlab = "Cytokine",
        las = 2,
        cex.axis = 0.8)
abline(h = c(0.3, 0.7), col = "gray", lty = 2, lwd = 1.5)
legend("topright", c("High (>0.7)", "Medium", "Low (<0.3)"), 
       lty = c(2, 0, 2), col = c("gray", NA, "gray"), cex = 0.7)
```

## Violin Plots

```{r violin, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Prepare data for ggplot
plot_df <- reshape2::melt(plot_data_box)
colnames(plot_df) <- c("Cell", "Cytokine", "Activity")

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Cytokine, y = Activity, fill = Cytokine)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.7, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.3, 0.7), linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Cytokine Activity Distributions (Violin Plot)",
       subtitle = "Showing density and quartiles",
       y = "Activity Score", x = "Cytokine")
```

## Density Plots

```{r density, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Activity, color = Cytokine, fill = Cytokine)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Activity Score Density Distributions",
       subtitle = "Comparing cytokine-specific patterns",
       x = "Activity Score", y = "Density")
```

# Correlation Analyses

## Cytokine-Cytokine Correlation

```{r correlation, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(activity_matrix, use = "complete.obs")

# Plot correlation heatmap
pheatmap(
  cor_matrix,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101),
  fontsize_row = 6,
  fontsize_col = 6,
  main = "Cytokine-Cytokine Activity Correlations",
  border_color = NA,
  clustering_distance_rows = "euclidean",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean"
)
```

## Correlation Network

```{r correlation_subset, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Focus on selected cytokines
selected_for_cor <- c("IL6", "IFNG", "IL4", "TNFA", "IL2", "IL10", "IL13", "IL17A")
cor_sub <- cor(activity_matrix[, selected_for_cor])

pheatmap(
  cor_sub,
  display_numbers = TRUE,
  number_format = "%.2f",
  fontsize_number = 9,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#67A9CF", "white", "#EF8A62"))(100),
  breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101),
  main = "Key Cytokine Correlations",
  border_color = "grey60",
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE
)
```

# Integration with Seurat

## Add Activities to Metadata

```{r metadata}
# Add top cytokines to Seurat metadata
top_cytokines <- c("IL6", "IFNG", "IL4", "TNFA")
for (cyt in top_cytokines) {
  pbmc_small <- AddMetaData(
    pbmc_small,
    metadata = activity_matrix[, cyt],
    col.name = paste0(cyt, "_activity")
  )
}
```

## Feature Plots

```{r featureplot, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Note: pbmc_small has no UMAP, so we'll create plots with available dimensions
# In real analysis with proper UMAP/tSNE, this would show spatial patterns

# Create a simple 2D projection for demonstration
set.seed(123)
pbmc_small@reductions$pca <- CreateDimReducObject(
  embeddings = matrix(rnorm(ncol(pbmc_small) * 2), ncol = 2),
  key = "PC_",
  assay = DefaultAssay(pbmc_small)
)

# Plot activities
FeaturePlot(pbmc_small, 
            features = paste0(top_cytokines, "_activity"),
            reduction = "pca",
            ncol = 2,
            cols = c("lightgrey", "blue")) &
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10))
```

## Ridge Plots by Cell Type

```{r ridgeplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
RidgePlot(pbmc_small, 
          features = paste0(top_cytokines[1:2], "_activity"),
          ncol = 1) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Violin Plots by Cell Type

```{r violinplot_seurat, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
VlnPlot(pbmc_small, 
        features = paste0(top_cytokines, "_activity"),
        ncol = 2,
        pt.size = 0.1) &
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Advanced Visualizations

## PCA of Cytokine Activities

```{r pca, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Perform PCA on cytokine activities
pca_result <- prcomp(activity_matrix, scale. = TRUE)

# Variance explained
var_explained <- (pca_result$sdev^2 / sum(pca_result$sdev^2))[1:10]

# Scree plot
barplot(var_explained * 100, 
        names.arg = 1:10,
        col = "steelblue",
        main = "PCA: Variance Explained by Components",
        xlab = "Principal Component",
        ylab = "Variance Explained (%)")

# Biplot
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(pca_result$x[, 1:2], 
     pch = 19, col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.5),
     main = "PCA: Cells in Cytokine Activity Space",
     xlab = sprintf("PC1 (%.1f%%)", var_explained[1]*100),
     ylab = sprintf("PC2 (%.1f%%)", var_explained[2]*100))

# Loading plot (top contributors)
loadings <- pca_result$rotation[, 1:2]
top_loadings <- order(abs(loadings[, 1]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]
plot(loadings[top_loadings, ], 
     pch = 19, col = "red",
     main = "Top 10 Cytokine Loadings",
     xlab = "PC1", ylab = "PC2")
text(loadings[top_loadings, ], 
     labels = rownames(loadings)[top_loadings],
     pos = 3, cex = 0.7)
abline(h = 0, v = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray")
```

## Hierarchical Clustering of Cells

```{r hierarchical, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# Cluster cells based on cytokine activities
dist_matrix <- dist(activity_matrix, method = "euclidean")
hc <- hclust(dist_matrix, method = "ward.D2")

# Plot dendrogram
plot(hc, labels = FALSE, hang = -1,
     main = "Hierarchical Clustering of Cells by Cytokine Activity",
     xlab = "Cells", ylab = "Height")
abline(h = mean(hc$height), col = "red", lty = 2)

# Cut tree into clusters
clusters <- cutree(hc, k = 3)
table(clusters)
```

## Heatmap with Cell Clustering

```{r heatmap_cell_clusters, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
# Add cluster annotation
cluster_annotation <- data.frame(
  Cluster = factor(clusters),
  row.names = rownames(activity_matrix)
)

# Select variable cytokines
top_var_cyts <- names(sort(apply(activity_matrix, 2, var), decreasing = TRUE)[1:30])

pheatmap(
  t(activity_matrix[, top_var_cyts]),
  annotation_col = cluster_annotation,
  fontsize_row = 6,
  fontsize_col = 4,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  main = "Cytokine Activities with Cell Clustering",
  border_color = NA
)
```

# Comparative Visualizations

## Compare Multiple Cytokines

```{r scatter_compare, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
# Scatter plot matrix for selected cytokines
pairs_cyts <- c("IL6", "IFNG", "IL4", "TNFA")
pairs_data <- activity_matrix[, pairs_cyts]

pairs(pairs_data,
      pch = 19,
      col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.3),
      main = "Cytokine Activity Relationships",
      upper.panel = NULL)
```

## IL6 vs IFNG Detailed Comparison

```{r scatter_detail, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
# Detailed scatter plot
plot_data_scatter <- data.frame(
  IL6 = activity_matrix[, "IL6"],
  IFNG = activity_matrix[, "IFNG"],
  CellType = Idents(pbmc_small)
)

ggplot(plot_data_scatter, aes(x = IL6, y = IFNG, color = CellType)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  labs(title = "IL6 vs IFNG Activity Comparison",
       subtitle = sprintf("Correlation: %.3f", cor(plot_data_scatter$IL6, plot_data_scatter$IFNG)),
       x = "IL6 Activity", y = "IFNG Activity")
```

# Summary Statistics Visualization

```{r summary_stats, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Calculate summary statistics
summary_stats <- data.frame(
  Cytokine = colnames(activity_matrix),
  Mean = apply(activity_matrix, 2, mean),
  Median = apply(activity_matrix, 2, median),
  SD = apply(activity_matrix, 2, sd),
  Min = apply(activity_matrix, 2, min),
  Max = apply(activity_matrix, 2, max)
)

# Sort by mean activity
summary_stats <- summary_stats[order(-summary_stats$Mean), ]
top_20 <- head(summary_stats, 20)

# Plot mean activities
par(mar = c(8, 4, 4, 2))
barplot(top_20$Mean,
        names.arg = top_20$Cytokine,
        las = 2,
        col = colorRampPalette(c("lightblue", "darkblue"))(20),
        main = "Top 20 Cytokines by Mean Activity",
        ylab = "Mean Activity Score",
        cex.names = 0.7)
abline(h = mean(activity_matrix), col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
legend("topright", "Overall Mean", lty = 2, col = "red", lwd = 2, cex = 0.8)
```

# Export-Quality Figures

## Publication-Ready Heatmap

```{r publication, fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
# Create a comprehensive publication figure
# Select top 30 variable cytokines
top_30_cyts <- names(sort(apply(activity_matrix, 2, var), decreasing = TRUE)[1:30])

# Prepare annotations
annotation_col <- data.frame(
  CellType = Idents(pbmc_small),
  row.names = colnames(pbmc_small)
)

# Create color schemes
ann_colors <- list(
  CellType = c("0" = "#E41A1C", "1" = "#377EB8", "2" = "#4DAF4A")
)

# Generate publication-quality heatmap
pheatmap(
  t(activity_matrix[, top_30_cyts]),
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  fontsize = 8,
  fontsize_row = 7,
  fontsize_col = 5,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  clustering_distance_rows = "correlation",
  clustering_distance_cols = "euclidean",
  color = colorRampPalette(c("#313695", "#FFFFFF", "#A50026"))(100),
  main = "Cytokine Activity Landscape in PBMC",
  show_colnames = FALSE,
  border_color = NA,
  cellwidth = 3,
  gaps_col = NULL
)
```

# Saving Plots

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
# Example: Save high-resolution figure
png("cytokine_heatmap.png", width = 3000, height = 2400, res = 300)
pheatmap(
  t(activity_matrix[, top_30_cyts]),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
  main = "Cytokine Activity Heatmap"
)
dev.off()

# Save as PDF
pdf("cytokine_heatmap.pdf", width = 10, height = 12)
pheatmap(
  t(activity_matrix[, top_30_cyts]),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100)
)
dev.off()
```

# Best Practices

## Visualization Guidelines

✅ **DO:**
- Use appropriate color schemes (diverging for signed data)
- Cluster to reveal patterns
- Annotate with cell types or conditions
- Show scale bars and legends
- Use consistent color scales across related plots

❌ **DON'T:**
- Over-plot (sample if >1000 cells)
- Use rainbow colors for continuous data
- Ignore outliers without justification
- Mix color schemes in multi-panel figures
